scope: First actual canonical run_profile over fixed official Source Web bundle/preset patches and staged current Cordis bindings
observations: The probe uses the real fixed Source CLI installation anchor and original package/bundle patch declarations. Only its process-local Native bindings and candidate version are substituted; production manifests, pin and accepted_upstream are unchanged.
Canonical startup rejected missing @deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node. Existing Python PTC is not silently substituted for a declared Node provider.

ClientModules rejected two missing account client bundles. The Native registry resolves these rows through its old workspace layout instead of the canonical Source runtime package router. This is a real resource ownership defect, not evidence that the original Source builds failed.

Current ClientModules Source also rereads manifest/bundle metadata on entry restart and uses stat-derived artifact revisions. Native still caches old metadata and uses opaque startup revisions; this contract is the next implementation part.

Because startup failed, the four preset-session creation attempts were not reached. No current Web, browser, preset or release acceptance follows from the attempted boot. The earlier old physical-preset duplicate-list_agents failures remain open until current composition is runnable.
diagnostics: Initial direct probe was stopped on noticing that only the launch option, not the process-level home, had been isolated. Owned PIDs 60536 and 67340 were terminated. Read-only no-follow metadata audit of the default DSH home found zero files modified since that probe began; no user files were removed or rewritten.

Second probe used an owned home in both locations but supplied a plain environment dict. Actual startup correctly exposed three consumers requiring LaunchEnvironmentSnapshot.get_from. The probe now supplies the real snapshot type; subsequent failed boot reports contain only the Node PTC and ClientModules failures.
Final receipt captures native/provider/script and Source input SHA-256 values and verifies Source tracked files remain clean after the attempted canonical run. No full release gate was run.
